newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX Hub natgas ends down but still in range.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX Hub natgas ends down but still in range.

text.p: NYMEX Henry Hub natgas futures mostly ended lower Tuesday in a moderate session, but reports of a firmer physical market despite moderate weather forecasts helped keep prices above technical support, sources said.
June slipped 3.4 cents to close at $2.215 per million British thermal units. July settled 1.9 cents lower at $2.246. Other deferreds ended steady to down by two cents.

"We're still waiting for a break of the trend. We came in strong, failed to make any progress and they jumped on it, but there was a lot of buying at $2.18 and $2.19 (basis June)," said one East Coast trader.

With cash still in the low-to-mid $2.20s despite mostly seasonal U.S. weather forecasts this week, most expected only limited downside from here, counting on steady injection demand to limit any pullback.

Technical traders agreed the market was range-bound, with support and resistance in June still pegged at $2.15 and $2.30, respectively. The broader range for June remained between the $2.05 double bottom and the $2.43 contract high.
Maintenance on Transco's Texas line will continue to cut about 400 million cubic feet per day (mmcfd) out of a total capacity of about 600 mmcfd Tuesday through Thursday.

In the cash, Gulf Coast swing prices firmed about a nickel Monday to the low-$2.20s. Midcon pipes were up a similar amount to the low-$2s. New York city gate gas was quoted more than five cents higher at about $2.50.
The NYMEX Henry Hub 12-month strip fell 1.7 cents to $2.26. NYMEX said 40,312 contracts traded, up from Friday's revised tally of 35,749.
On the KCBT, June finished 0.6 cent lower at $2.065, while deferreds ended steady to up by one cent. The East/West spread narrowed by 2.8 cents to 15.0 cents (NYMEX premium).
